$comment: ART's own map from an ADOPTED install-media row (media_hashes.json, rootrootde/emu68hatcher, MIT) to the artefact id ART's slots are named by. It exists because the adopted table stays exactly as adopted -- mediahash.rs's own rule, so a reader can tell whose claim a row is -- and Hatcher's data names no ART id. Writing an `artefact` field into his rows would be putting ART's bookkeeping into somebody else's claim; shadowing them with duplicate rows in media_hashes_own.json would be the silent-first-wins that module's design forbids. So the join lives here, keyed on the two fields the adopted rows do state about themselves: `version` and `volume` (Hatcher's own identifier for the disk -- NEVER the AmigaDOS volume name a disk states on its root block; see MediaRow::volume for the measurement that separates the two namespaces). Read 2026-09-08 out of media_hashes.json itself: the four AmigaOS 3.9 identifiers below cover all seven of its 3.9 rows -- four ISO masterings under AmigaOS3_9, one BoingBag 1, one BoingBag 2 and one BoingBags 3&4, every one sourced 'Haage and Partners (3.9)'. slots.rs's every_adopted_3_9_row_maps_to_an_artefact re-checks that against the real file rather than against this comment. `boingbags-39-3-4` named an artefact ART shipped no recipe for when this file was written, and round 3 shipped one (`recipes/packages/boingbags-39-3-4.json`), so the slot list now does ask for it. The rule the entry was recording still holds and is why it was written before the recipe existed: an id here is a name for **bytes**, not a claim that ART can install them -- BoingBags 3&4 is registered `not_yet_runnable` and refused for host placement, and this row is what lets its slot find the file and name it all the same. `filenames` (fix round 1) is ART's own claim about the same artefacts, and it lives here for the same reason the id does: the adopted table carries no such field on any of its 186 rows and is not going to gain one. Without it the AmigaOS 3.9 BoingBag 2 slot -- whose only row is adopted -- had a not-found sentence with its actionable half missing, naming no file for the user to go and obtain. A name here is a hint for the drop-folder guide and for the weakest match rank, never a requirement: a file can carry any name on disk and still be these bytes.

artefacts._why_directories: Design 3.6's structural check beside the hash, built 2026-09-08 (round 2 whole-branch review, L6). Three directories the AmigaOS 3.9 CD carries at its root; a disc whose bytes ART recognises but whose root is missing one of them is a re-master or a partial copy, and the readout says 'matched but incomplete: <dir> missing' rather than 'not found' -- two different next steps, and telling somebody a disc is absent when it is sitting in the folder is this project's named defect. ART's own claim, like `filenames` above and for the same reason: the adopted table says nothing about any disc's contents. The list is deliberately short -- these three are the ones the design names and the ones every reader of the 3.9 CD in ART actually reads from; a longer list would turn an unusual-but-usable mastering into a warning.
